clue.text: A cold mixture of Brie and cranberries initially used in tart

parts.note: C is the standard abbreviation for cold, as on a tap

indicators.note: a mixture stirs things together, so the letters of the cheese are jumbled
initially points to the opening letter of the word cranberries

explanation.surface: A recipe for a chilled tart filled with Brie and cranberries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixture of' turns BRIE into ERBI; the tart of the surface is a pastry, but the definition is the adjective meaning sharp.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a sharp, biting taste or manner of speaking, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Have belief in deed enshrining church power

indicators.note: enshrining means enclosing as in a shrine, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: an act is a deed
CE stands for Church of England
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A document that preserves the authority of the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a claim is to believe it, to have faith in it.

clue.text: One giving authority's defensible, though not at first right

indicators.note: not at first means the opening letter is removed

parts.note: a tenable position is one that can be defended

explanation.surface: An official's argument holds up, though it was initially not correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not at first' strips TENABLE down to ENABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: An enabler is someone who empowers another, giving them the means or authority to act.

clue.text: Pounds over each part of London

indicators.note: in a down clue over means placed above, so the first piece comes before the second

parts.note: batters means strikes repeatedly, pounds

explanation.surface: Money spent on every district of the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: Pounds looks like money, but it is the verb. BATTERSEA is a district of south London on the Thames.
explanation.definitionFit: Battersea is a district of south London, known for its power station and dogs' home.

clue.text: How Parisian schedule upset political correspondent?

parts.note: comment is the French for how, as a Parisian would say it

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a rota is a schedule of duties

explanation.surface: Wondering how a French politician's diary got disrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: A political correspondent is a journalist who offers commentary, a kind of commentator.

clue.text: Pretended most of quantity of water's a detergent

parts.note: to sham is to pretend, and sham works as the past sense here

indicators.note: most of a word means dropping its final letter

parts.note: a pool is a small body of standing water

explanation.surface: Someone faked using a pool's worth of water and called it a cleaning product.
explanation.definitionFit: Shampoo is a soapy cleansing liquid, a kind of detergent for hair or carpets.

clue.text: Very new boy

parts.note: so means very, as in so good

explanation.surface: A really fresh young lad.
explanation.definitionFit: A son is a male child, a boy.

clue.text: Element of technical language avoided by judge

indicators.note: avoided by means the named letter is left out

parts.note: jargon is specialist technical language

explanation.surface: A judge steers clear of a piece of legal jargon.
explanation.definitionFit: Argon is a chemical element, one of the noble gases.

clue.text: Participant in (and curtailer of) seaside show

definitions.text: Participant in (and curtailer of) seaside show

parts.words: Participant in (and curtailer of) seaside show
parts.note: a clown in a white costume performing in a seaside troupe; split in two it is decay of a pier, which would end a show staged there

explanation.surface: A performer who takes part in, and puts a stop to, a summer show by the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: British resorts had end-of-the-pier shows by troupes of white-faced clowns; read as PIER ROT, the word names the decay that would shut such a show down.
explanation.definitionFit: A pierrot is a white-costumed clown of the old seaside entertainment troupes.

clue.text: Play round more tidily, bagging first in Carnoustie

parts.note: O is round in shape

indicators.note: bagging means capturing, so the outer word holds the letter

parts.note: neater means in a tidier way

indicators.note: first in points to the opening letter of Carnoustie

explanation.surface: A golfer plays a round more neatly, picking up a win at Carnoustie.
explanation.walkthrough: Carnoustie is a famous Scottish golf course, so play and round suggest golf.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-acter is a short play in a single act.

clue.text: Carpenter, say, ship's one, pulled out of sea

parts.note: a craft is a ship or boat, here in the possessive
a man overboard who is hauled back aboard is one pulled out of the sea, so the phrase gives a man

explanation.surface: A sailor is rescued from the waves after falling off a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A carpenter is an example of a skilled manual worker, a craftsman; 'say' marks it as an example.

clue.text: Protectors of city, say, about to observe retreating

indicators.note: retreating means moving backwards, so the built letters are read in reverse
about means going round, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: e.g. (for example) is the usual short form of say
to observe is to see

explanation.surface: Guards of a city are about to watch a withdrawal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'retreating' work in turn, giving ESEEG then its reverse. Legend says the sacred geese of the Capitol in ancient Rome woke the guards when the Gauls attacked.
explanation.definitionFit: Roman legend says cackling sacred geese warned the city of a night attack, so they were its protectors.

clue.text: Cry pitifully, receiving second beating

indicators.note: receiving means taking something in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to pule is to whimper or whine feebly

explanation.surface: Someone whimpers as they take a second thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A pulse is the rhythmic beating of the heart felt in the arteries.

clue.text: Somewhat peculiar chap hoarding country's principal coin

indicators.note: hoarding means holding something inside, so the name wraps the other letters

parts.note: Eric is a man's name, a typical chap

indicators.note: principal means chief or first, so the opening letter of country is taken

parts.note: a cent is a small coin

explanation.surface: An odd fellow stockpiles the main currency of his country.
explanation.definitionFit: Eccentric means odd or unconventional, a near synonym of peculiar.

clue.text: Papers getting centralised distribution

indicators.note: distribution spreads things around, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Documents handed out by a central office.
explanation.definitionFit: Credentials are documents proving identity or qualifications, papers.

clue.text: Take a tough decision to do some weeding?

definitions.meaning: an idiom meaning to tackle a difficult matter boldly
literally, gripping a stinging weed firmly in order to pull it up

explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means facing up to an unpleasant task, and literally means seizing a stinging plant.

clue.text: Complicated package sent up — zero charge added

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means moved upwards, so the word reads backwards

parts.note: a bale is a large bound package of goods
O looks like zero
a rate is a charge or price

explanation.surface: A tricky parcel posted with no extra fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Elaborate means detailed and intricate, therefore complicated.

clue.text: Small piece in column at foot of page

indicators.note: in a down clue, at the foot of means placed below, so the column comes after the page letter

parts.note: a newspaper column is an article

explanation.surface: A short item printed in a column at the bottom of a newspaper page.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a tiny fragment or speck, a small piece.

clue.text: Marxist view of betting opportunities?

parts.note: read as the title of a Marx Brothers film comedy set at a racetrack, rather than political theory about gambling

explanation.surface: A communist philosopher's take on the bookmakers' odds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marxist' suggests Karl Marx, but it means the Marx Brothers, whose 1937 film is set around horse racing.
explanation.definitionFit: The film title names an outing to the horse racing, where betting opportunities abound.

clue.text: Praise a paired couple of pianos, once set up

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, so two pianos are PP

indicators.note: once set up means when raised in a down clue, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: dual means paired, made of two

explanation.surface: Applause for a duo playing two pianos once they are set up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'once set up' turns DUAL into LAUD.
explanation.definitionFit: To applaud is to praise or express approval, literally by clapping.

clue.text: Flexible line accepted by bridge-player in clubs to start with

indicators.note: accepted by means taken in, so the line letter goes inside

parts.note: East is one of the four players at bridge

indicators.note: to start with points to the opening letters of in and clubs

explanation.surface: A versatile bid accepted by a bridge player who leads in clubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic means stretchy and springy, flexible.

clue.text: Engineer tangible output from harvest?

parts.note: CE stands for civil engineer
real means tangible, actual

explanation.surface: An engineer produces real results from the harvest.
explanation.definitionFit: Cereal grain is what a harvest produces, its output.

clue.text: Exponent of spin about to enter party? That's classified

parts.note: a spinning top is something that demonstrates spin

indicators.note: to enter means to go inside, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: a sect is a faction or party
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor is about to join a party, and that news is confidential.
explanation.definitionFit: Classified documents are officially secret; the phrase is the highest such grading.

clue.text: Go into American heartland, shunning cold

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so a letter is left out

parts.note: center is the American spelling of centre, the heart of something

explanation.surface: Travel into the middle of the USA, avoiding the cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To enter is to go into a place.

clue.text: Speak in florid style, ignoring note

indicators.note: ignoring means leaving out, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: ornate means elaborately decorated, florid

explanation.surface: Advice to talk flamboyantly while disregarding a written memo.
explanation.definitionFit: To orate is to make a formal speech, often pompously, so it means to speak.

clue.text: A few words about river map

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the talk goes round the other letter

parts.note: a chat is a brief informal talk, a few words

explanation.surface: A short talk concerning a map of a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A chart is a map, especially one used for navigation at sea.

clue.text: Argue wildly about stake-money and get assurance

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the stake
wildly suggests disorder, so the letters of argue are rearranged

parts.note: an ante is the stake put up before a hand of poker

explanation.surface: Gamblers row furiously over the stake and are given a promise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' makes GUARE, and 'about' wraps that round the stake; 'Argue' looks like the start of a quarrel between gamblers.
explanation.definitionFit: A guarantee is a formal assurance that something will be done.

clue.text: Stay to tease bloke

definitions.meaning: a rope or wire that holds a tent or mast steady

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a supporting rope, to mock playfully, and a man: three senses.

clue.text: Old tree latterly becoming hollow?

parts.note: the elder is a small tree with dark berries

indicators.note: a word made hollow loses its inside, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An ancient tree has recently developed a hollow trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Elderly means old, said of people past middle age.

clue.text: Scent disaster — one pound in office plate

indicators.note: a disaster leaves things in ruins, so the letters of scent are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
L is the abbreviation for pound, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A bad smell costing a pound in a workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: A stencil is a cut sheet or plate used in offices to reproduce lettering.
